output.name: Halun

anatomy.part: end of the trailing string, where the waiting girl holds it

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the gulls flew after the sky and came home with nothing but cold in their feathers. So Ennu the Kite-Wright wove a gull from sailcloth and bone, so that someone on the islands could still be seen from Vel. Halun was the first of these. Each evening, when the boats were out, a young woman flew it from the high rock above the harbour. A young man who wanted her rowed under the cliff, and if the gull dipped one wing toward the water, he might climb. Mother Hesk keeps count of such things. One evening Tavo came down the sound, laughing, and tore the cloth away with the string. The girl stood on the rock until the boats came in, her hands still making the shape of a pull. Halun is up there yet, waiting for a rope that was never tugged.
output.verse:
Halun waits on wind,
her gull-kite pulls at cold rope.
He rows. She waits still.
